subject: body
title: The Five Senses
about: The five senses and the body part for each: eyes see, ears hear, nose smells, tongue tastes and skin feels; which sense tells him the soup is hot, the music is loud, the honey is sweet or the cookies smell good; how senses keep him safe (smelling smoke, hearing a car, reading a stop sign, spitting out something strange that is not food); senses working as a team; and the kind truth that people who cannot see or hear use their other senses and tools like a white cane, hearing aids, braille and sign language, and how he can help a friend who cannot hear well. The five senses are a classic early-grades science topic that NC's 2023 Grade 1 science standards do not name, so this is a bridge topic tagged to 1.PCH.2.1 and 1.PCH.2.2 (noticing danger such as smoke), 1.ICHR.1.2 (what makes each person special) and Science PS.1.1.2 (observing and comparing with the senses). Read it together: every question and choice is read aloud.
tip: Play a guessing game with his eyes closed: a spoon, a sock, a lemon. Which sense told him what it was?

cards.q: Which body part do you taste with?
cards.note: Tiny taste buds all over your tongue sort out sweet, salty, sour and bitter. Lick a lemon and the sour ones get busy.

cards.q: The music is very loud. Which body part tells you that?
cards.note: Ears catch sounds. Very loud sounds can hurt them, so turn the music down.

cards.q: Which body part do you smell with?
cards.note: Air carries tiny bits of smell into your nose when you breathe in.

cards.q: A big red sign says STOP. Which sense reads it for you?
cards.note: Sight means seeing. Your eyes read signs, lights and faces so you know what to do.

cards.q: One sense works all over your body, in your skin. Which sense is it?
cards.note: Skin feels soft and rough, hot and cold, tickles and hugs.

cards.q: You hold an ice cube and it feels cold. Which body part felt that?
cards.note: Your skin feels hot and cold so you can pull away from things that could hurt you.

cards.q: Cookies are baking and the house smells yummy. Which sense is that?
cards.note: Smells float through the air into your nose, even from another room.

cards.q: Honey is sweet and a pickle is sour. Which sense tells them apart?
cards.note: Sweet and sour are two of the four tastes your tongue knows. Smell helps too, so food tastes dull when your nose is stuffy.

cards.q: You take a tiny sip and the soup is too hot. Which parts felt the heat?
cards.note: Lips and tongue feel hot and cold just like skin does. Blow on hot food and wait.

cards.q: Your friend cannot hear well. How can you help them understand you?
cards.note: Seeing your face and lips helps a lot. Speak clearly, and never shout.

cards.q: You smell smoke in the house. What should you do?
cards.note: Your nose can warn you before your eyes see fire. Smelling smoke means get a grown-up right away.

cards.q: You hear a car coming before you step into the street. Which sense kept you safe?
cards.note: Stop, look and listen. Your ears can hear a car even when it is around the corner.

cards.q: A person who cannot see well may carry a long white cane. What is the cane for?
cards.note: The cane taps the ground to find steps and curbs before the feet get there. A guide dog can help too.

cards.q: Some people's ears hear sounds very softly. What makes sounds louder for them?
cards.note: A hearing aid is a tiny speaker that sits in or behind the ear.

cards.q: A person who cannot see can read a book with bumpy dots. What do they read with?
cards.note: The dots are called braille, and fingertips feel each letter. Touch does the job that eyes usually do.

cards.q: Some people who cannot hear talk with their hands. What is that called?
cards.note: Sign language uses hand shapes and faces to say words. You can learn some too.

cards.q: You see a dog's tail wag and hear it bark. How many senses are you using?
cards.note: Sight and hearing. Your senses work as a team, and your brain puts the messages together.

cards.q: You put something strange in your mouth and it tastes nasty. What do you do?
cards.note: A nasty taste from something that is not food can be your body's warning. Spit it out and tell a grown-up what it was.
